done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates and date ranges, plus a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

dismissals.because: backend/src/chat/chat.service.ts:388 'by FY for July 2026' mixes fiscal grouping with a calendar month, a phrasing edge case; on 2026-10-02 the owner ruled the date coverage sufficient and asked to close this fix as it stands (handoff and conversation), and in this case the answer falls back to the model's window, the pre-fix behaviour, not a wrong deterministic period

backend/src/chat/chat.service.ts:741 'amount as 2025' is another phrasing edge case of the same open-ended family; the owner ruled the coverage sufficient on 2026-10-02 and asked to close the fix, and the 98+ phrasings already in the table cover the common amount forms (copulas, comparisons, currency, units, grouping, quantity nouns)

backend/src/chat/chat.service.test.ts:453 the repository has no Playwright suite and adding one is outside a five-file fix; the user-flow proof is the walked functional check recorded in commit 03d49e0 (and a195a8b), driven through the running frontend, API and the real July warehouse with the host Bedrock model: the three-turn July thread, the no-period inheritance, 'What about August?', and switching an answer's period to FY YTD, which is Forge's functional-check contract

findings.body: Unlike the previously reported fiscal-period case, `by FY` is granularity wording: `FISCAL_GRANULARITY_PATTERN` explicitly removes it when deciding whether a question names a period. However, this earlier check uses the unmodified question. Consequently, a follow-up such as “Show Actual by FY for July 2026” sets `parsedTimeWindow` to null merely because it contains `FY`; `hasTimePeriodWords` then sees July and retains whatever window the model emitted instead of applying July 2026. This violates the requirement that an app-readable named period win regardless of the model window.
findings.title: Not done: fiscal grouping can suppress a named calendar period

findings.body: The amount disambiguator omits the common linking word `as`. For example, “Show Actual with amount as 2025” reaches `calendarYear`; neither the direct-quantity check nor `LINKED_AMOUNT_YEAR_PATTERN` recognizes the text before 2025, so the code constructs a full-year 2025 window and overrides the model/prior window. This contradicts the explicit requirement that an amount is never read as a year.
findings.title: Not done: “amount as 2025” is still parsed as calendar year 2025

findings.body: The added matrix and rerun checks still call `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, whose provider, executor/warehouse, audit, dimensions, reports, and resolver are fakes (around lines 1303–1333). The registered test command runs Node tests and Vitest, and the repository has no Playwright flow through a running API, real database, and browser. Thus named-period precedence, inheritance, amount protection, and period-control reruns remain proven only at mocked service/jsdom boundaries. The supplied successful close run executed those same non-E2E commands, so the prior blocker remains open.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
